\textbf{\large Monotonic Sequences Worksheet --- Solutions}

\vspace{8pt}

\typehead{Type A: The Difference Test}{Use the difference $a_{n+1} - a_n$ to show that the given sequence $\{a_n\}$ is strictly increasing or strictly decreasing.}

\problem{1.}{\left\{ 3 - \frac{2}{n} \right\}_{n=1}^{+\infty}}

$a_n = 3 - \dfrac{2}{n}$, so $a_{n+1} = 3 - \dfrac{2}{n+1}$.
$$
a_{n+1} - a_n = \left(3 - \frac{2}{n+1}\right) - \left(3 - \frac{2}{n}\right)
= \frac{2}{n} - \frac{2}{n+1}
= \frac{2(n+1) - 2n}{n(n+1)}
= \frac{2}{n(n+1)} > 0 \quad \text{for all } n \ge 1.
$$
Since $a_{n+1} - a_n > 0$, we have $a_{n+1} > a_n$ for all $n$.

\answer{increasing}

\problem{2.}{\left\{ \frac{n}{5n - 2} \right\}_{n=1}^{+\infty}}

$a_n = \dfrac{n}{5n-2}$, so $a_{n+1} = \dfrac{n+1}{5(n+1)-2} = \dfrac{n+1}{5n+3}$.
$$
\begin{aligned}
a_{n+1} - a_n &= \frac{n+1}{5n+3} - \frac{n}{5n-2}
= \frac{(n+1)(5n-2) - n(5n+3)}{(5n+3)(5n-2)} \\
&= \frac{(5n^2 + 3n - 2) - (5n^2 + 3n)}{(5n+3)(5n-2)}
= \frac{-2}{(5n+3)(5n-2)}.
\end{aligned}
$$
For $n \ge 1$, both $5n+3 > 0$ and $5n-2 > 0$, so $a_{n+1} - a_n < 0$, i.e. $a_{n+1} < a_n$.

\answer{decreasing}

\problem{3.}{\left\{ n - 3^{n} \right\}_{n=1}^{+\infty}}

$a_n = n - 3^n$, so $a_{n+1} = (n+1) - 3^{n+1}$.
$$
a_{n+1} - a_n = \big[(n+1) - 3^{n+1}\big] - \big[n - 3^n\big]
= 1 - 3^{n+1} + 3^n
= 1 - 3\cdot 3^n + 3^n
= 1 - 2\cdot 3^n.
$$
For $n \ge 1$, $2 \cdot 3^n \ge 6 > 1$, so $a_{n+1} - a_n < 0$, i.e. $a_{n+1} < a_n$.

\answer{decreasing}

\newpage

\typehead{Type B: The Ratio Test}{Use the ratio $a_{n+1} / a_n$ to show that the given sequence $\{a_n\}$ is strictly increasing or strictly decreasing. All terms of these sequences are positive.}

\problem{4.}{\left\{ \frac{3^{n}}{2 + 3^{n}} \right\}_{n=1}^{+\infty}}

$a_n = \dfrac{3^n}{2+3^n}$, so $a_{n+1} = \dfrac{3^{n+1}}{2+3^{n+1}}$.
$$
\frac{a_{n+1}}{a_n} = \frac{3^{n+1}}{2+3^{n+1}} \cdot \frac{2+3^n}{3^n}
= \frac{3(2+3^n)}{2+3^{n+1}}
= \frac{6 + 3^{n+1}}{2 + 3^{n+1}}.
$$
The numerator is larger than the denominator ($6 > 2$), so $\dfrac{a_{n+1}}{a_n} > 1$, i.e. $a_{n+1} > a_n$.

\answer{increasing}

\problem{5.}{\left\{ \frac{n}{3^{n}} \right\}_{n=1}^{+\infty}}

$a_n = \dfrac{n}{3^n}$, so $a_{n+1} = \dfrac{n+1}{3^{n+1}}$.
$$
\frac{a_{n+1}}{a_n} = \frac{n+1}{3^{n+1}} \cdot \frac{3^n}{n} = \frac{n+1}{3n}.
$$
For $n \ge 1$: $\; n + 1 \le 2n < 3n$, so $\dfrac{a_{n+1}}{a_n} = \dfrac{n+1}{3n} < 1$, i.e. $a_{n+1} < a_n$.

\answer{decreasing}

\problem{6.}{\left\{ \frac{(2n)!}{(n!)^{2}} \right\}_{n=1}^{+\infty}}

$a_n = \dfrac{(2n)!}{(n!)^2}$, so $a_{n+1} = \dfrac{(2n+2)!}{\big((n+1)!\big)^2}$. Using $(2n+2)! = (2n+2)(2n+1)\,(2n)!$ and $(n+1)! = (n+1)\,n!$:
$$
\frac{a_{n+1}}{a_n} = \frac{(2n+2)(2n+1)\,(2n)!}{(n+1)^2\,(n!)^2} \cdot \frac{(n!)^2}{(2n)!}
= \frac{(2n+2)(2n+1)}{(n+1)^2}
= \frac{2(n+1)(2n+1)}{(n+1)^2}
= \frac{2(2n+1)}{n+1} = \frac{4n+2}{n+1}.
$$
Since $4n + 2 > n + 1$ for $n \ge 1$, $\dfrac{a_{n+1}}{a_n} > 1$, i.e. $a_{n+1} > a_n$.

\answer{increasing}
